items.followUp: What is volatile memory? Give one example.

rubric.why: Non-volatile memory keeps its data when power is removed.
rubric.description: Explains that the memory retains data without power.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that its data is retained when power is off.

rubric.why: ROM and flash memory are examples of non-volatile memory.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any valid example, such as ROM or flash memory.

modelAnswer: Non-volatile memory retains its data even when the power is switched off.
Examples include ROM and flash memory.

rubric.why: Phishing relies on deception, often through a fake message or website.
rubric.description: Identifies phishing as a deceptive attempt or use of a fake email or website.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing its deceptive method.

rubric.why: The attacker aims to obtain private or valuable information.
rubric.description: States that phishing tries to steal sensitive information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the information the attacker seeks.

modelAnswer: A phishing attack is a deceptive attempt, often using a fake email or website, to trick a person.
Its purpose is to steal sensitive information such as passwords or bank details.

items.followUp: Name one example of a guided communication medium and one example of an unguided medium.

rubric.why: Guided is one of the two main types of communication medium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming guided media.

rubric.why: Unguided is the other main type of communication medium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming unguided media.

modelAnswer: The two main types of communication medium are guided (wired) and unguided (wireless).
Examples include twisted-pair, coaxial, or fibre-optic cable for guided media, and radio waves or microwaves for unguided media.
